 OP(Crl.)No.776 of 2025 2 2025:KER:93564  JUDGMENT
The original petitioners herein are the petitioners and the respondents are the respondents in M.C.No.26/2024 on the files of Family Court, Kunnamkulam.
The said M.C. is filed under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. (Section 144 of BNSS).
The said case was referred to mediation, in which all the disputes pending between the parties were settled and Ext.P2 mediation agreement was entered into between the parties.
The grievance of the petitioner is that the Family Court is not accepting Ext.P2 and disposing of the case in its terms.
It is in these circumstances, the petitioners have approached this Court.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for the respondents.

3. Apart from M.C.No.26/2024, two other cases are also pending before the same Family Court; (i)
O.P.No.2568/2023 for return of money and gold OP(Crl.)No.776 of 2025 3 2025:KER:93564 ornaments and (ii) G.O.P.No.528/2024 for custody of the child.

Two other cases between the parties;
(i)C.C.No.199/2024 is pending before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Irinjalakuda and (ii)M.C.No.115/2023 is pending before the Magistrate Court, Vadakkancherry.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Irinjalakuda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In C.C.No.199/2024,
the respondent is the accused and the offence is under Section 498 A of IPC.
M.C.No.115/2023, is a case under the provisions of the Domestic Violence Act.
4. I have called for remarks from the Family Court as to why Ext.P2 mediation agreement was not accepted.
The learned Judge of the Family Court gave a report stating that, only M.C.No.26/2024 was referred for mediation.
The terms of the agreement include the settlement of other cases as well.
5. I went through Ext.P2.
It would show that the entire disputes between the parties in all the cases were settled.
It is true that M.C.No.26/2024 alone was referred to mediation.

However, there is no bar in OP(Crl.)No.776 of 2025 4 2025:KER:93564 settling the entire disputes between the parties,
even though only one dispute was referred to mediation.
O.P.No.2568/2023 and G.O.P.No.528/2024 are pending before the same Family Court.
Therefore, there is no difficulty in recording the compromise in all the three cases together.
So far as M.C.No.115/2023 is concerned, it is submitted that the said case has already been withdrawn.
The learned counsel for the respondent submitted that the offence involved in C.C.No.199/2024 is under Section 498A of IPC.

The Supreme Court in K. Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa [(2013) 5 SCC 226] has held that though offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC is not compoundable, in appropriate cases, if the parties are willing and if it appears to the Court that there exist elements of settlement, it should direct the parties to explore the possibility of settlement through mediation.

entities.text: K. Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa [(2013) 5 SCC 226]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further held that for the settlement to come through, the parties can approach the High Court and get the appropriate order.

Hence, there Shaheema vs Ajeeb.P.H on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160964485/
2 is absolutely OP(Crl.)No.776 of 2025 5 2025:KER:93564 no bar to incorporate the settlement with respect to C.C.No.199/2024 also in the mediation agreement.
All the terms of mediation agreement appears to be voluntary.

Hence, the Family Court is directed to take M.C.No.26/2024,
O.P.No.2568/2023 and G.O.P.No.528/ 2024 together and record Ext.P2 compromise therein and dispose of the matter in accordance with law.
OP(Crl) is disposed of as above.
Sd/-
